family_projection_rules.notes: Auth is canonical. Auth is not session. Provider session is not YAI session. Auth posture does not imply entitlement, machine authorization, license lease, runtime gate, case, operator context, or client/shell attachment.

Case is canonical for case-tree truth. Active case belongs to operator context, not session. `case.enter`, `case.leave`, and `case.status` remain public CLI/TUI projections, while explicit API ownership of active-case posture lives under `operator_context`.

Operator context is the canonical API family for active-case selection posture. It owns `active_case_ref` and does not own auth, authorization, runtime lifecycle, client attachment, or shell attachment.
Compatibility only. Session is not a canonical public domain family after V51.
`flow` is retained only as a legacy alias and must not be reintroduced as a canonical API family.
Root records is not a canonical public family. State owns canonical record query/tail operations.
Plural API family is preserved while CLI/TUI may project singular names.
Plural API family is preserved while CLI/TUI may project singular names.
Plural API family is preserved while CLI/TUI may project singular names.
API family stays underscore-based while CLI/TUI may render the hyphenated spelling.
API family stays noun-based while CLI/TUI may use the verb `materialize`.
Lineage is first-class in V51. `knowledge.lineage.*` is compatibility-only where retained.
Evidence is first-class in V51. `control.evidence.*` is compatibility-only where retained.
Logs must stay scoped to runtime/job/workflow/agent/provider. Generic root logs ownership is forbidden.

legacy_alias_mappings.notes: Use `auth.context.inspect` for safe auth-context posture instead of legacy `whoami` wording.
Use `case.open` for nested case manifest creation or ensure semantics. `case.create` is older naming.
Use `case.enter` for operator-context active-case selection. `case.use` predates the explicit operator-context split.
Flow remains a compatibility alias only.
Compatibility trace retained while lineage becomes first-class.
Compatibility evidence projection retained while evidence becomes first-class.
No single replacement family exists. Replacement meaning is split across auth, case/context, client/shell, and system surfaces.
Root records is transitional only; state.records is canonical.
Runtime status remains a CLI/TUI compatibility projection over canonical system status.
Use `policy_pack.*` or `governance.policy.resolve` instead of a root policy family.
Use recall or family-local query surfaces instead of a root query family.
Use family-local inspect operations instead of a root inspect family.

projection_bridges.notes: `yai case enter <case>` remains the primary CLI projection while API ownership of active-case mutation lives under `operator_context`.
`yai case leave` remains the primary CLI projection while API ownership of active-case clearing lives under `operator_context`.
`yai case status` remains a public posture view while explicit active-case ownership is surfaced under `operator_context`.
Future `yai context switch <case>` projects the same active-case mutation boundary.
Future `yai context clear` projects the same active-case clear boundary.
